subject: Outbound lock-step: private endpoint allowlist & firewall playbook
messages:
From: security@bluenovahealth.com
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: devops+bluenova@bluenovahealth.com
Date: 2028-05-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Request: definitive allowlist & firewall requirements for private endpoint POC

Hi Sofia,

We are preparing a private deployment (VPC-attached) of Redwood Private for our inference gateway and need a single canonical set of requirements to share with our network/security teams. Specifically we need: 1) a concrete list of outbound IPs/ports for allowlisting (production and fallback), 2) expected SNI/FQDNs and TLS behavior, 3) guidance on NAT vs. static egress, and 4) what telemetry/log evidence Redwood can provide for audits.

Can you send a short playbook or checklist we can use for our firewall and change window? We are aiming to begin firewall changes the week of May 22.

Thanks —
Aaron Li
Security Engineer, BlueNova Health
security@bluenovahealth.com

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: security@bluenovahealth.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: definitive allowlist & firewall requirements for private endpoint POC

Thanks Aaron — I can consolidate a playbook. High-level notes up front: we try to keep outbound dependence minimal and provide multiple fallback paths (static egress, region fallback, model-variant failover). Below is an initial plan; David will add the port/IP specifics and a CSV of the candidate egress IPs.

Short plan:  
- Provide two tiers of allowlist: minimal (control plane + model fetch) and expanded (telemetry, metrics, artifact fetch).
- Prefer static/pinned egress IPs for production; ephemeral NAT is acceptable for POC if you also allow the resolver FQDNs and expect short-lived changes.
- Use SNI-based FQDN allowlisting for service-level routing but require IPs for firewall-level enforcement if you must.
- We can provide TLS server cert fingerprints and signed evidence of our SOC2 controls on request.

I'll attach the playbook draft once David uploads the egress manifest. Proposed next steps: 1) David to send IP/port matrix, 2) your network team to confirm whether perimeter only accepts IPs or FQDN+SNI, 3) we run a short connectivity test (10–15 min) during the change window.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
PM, Integrations — Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, security@bluenovahealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-13T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: definitive allowlist & firewall requirements for private endpoint POC

Aaron / team — attaching the egress-ip-manifest.csv (stub) and a technical checklist below. This is the recommended configuration for a VPC-onprem connector using our private endpoint runtime.

Attachment: egress-ip-manifest.csv (columns: role, ip, port, proto, comment)

Technical checklist (concise):
- Control plane (account provisioning, model catalog updates):
  - IPs: 18.197.24.101, 18.197.24.102 (primary / warm-failover)
  - Ports: 443 outbound (HTTPS).
  - FQDNs: control.redwood-inference.com (SNI: control.redwood-inference.com)

- Model fetch & artifact storage:
  - IPs: 52.214.13.7 (artifact CDN edge), 52.214.13.8 (geo-failover)
  - Ports: 443 outbound; TLS mutual auth optional for high-security setups.

- Telemetry & metrics (optional expanded allowlist):
  - FQDNs: telemetry.redwood-inference.com; prefer FQDN/SNI allowlisting.
  - Ports: 443; supports proxying through your company telemetry endpoint if needed.

- NAT vs static IP guidance:
  - POC: ephemeral NAT is OK if your firewall team is comfortable with FQDN/SNI allowlisting and you accept short DNS TTLs (~60s).
  - Production (recommended): reserve/pin the static egress IPs we provide and put them in your perimeter allowlist. Static IPs allow consistent audit trails.

- Certificate & TLS expectations:
  - TLS 1.2+ required; prefer TLS 1.3.
  - Server certificate CN = service FQDN; we publish cert fingerprints for the control plane.
  - SNI is used for routing; if firewall only allows IPs, we will coordinate IP handoffs during the change window.

- Audit & evidence we can provide:
  - Per-request logs (ingress timestamp, egress target, model id) retained for 90 days by default.
  - Per-tenant telemetry snapshots and signed attestations for SOC2 evidence.
  - Connectivity test script (curl-based) and packet capture sample for the ops window.

I'll mark the manifest as draft until we confirm BlueNova's preferred IP binding strategy.

— David
David Kim
Staff Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: devops+bluenova@bluenovahealth.com
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: ciso@bluenovahealth.com
Date: 2028-05-14T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: definitive allowlist & firewall requirements for private endpoint POC

Thanks David — a few clarifying questions from our network/security leads:  
1) Can Redwood support an intermediate translation hop? Our perimeter requires all outbound to originate from a fixed NAT gateway maintained by our central cloud team. If so, we need to know whether you will accept TLS passthrough to the NATted IPs or whether you require direct source IP validation.
2) How does Redwood handle ephemeral IP rotation? If you rotate egress IPs, how much lead time do you provide and can you pin a stable domain that resolves to current egress addresses?
3) For audit purposes we need signed evidence that calls made during the change window came from the claimed tenant. Is there a recommended header or TLS client cert attribute we should check in logs?

We attached our security questionnaire for your compliance team.

— Ravi Patel
Senior Cloud Engineer, BlueNova Health
Attachment: security-questionnaire.pdf

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
To: devops+bluenova@bluenovahealth.com, security@bluenovahealth.com
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-15T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: definitive allowlist & firewall requirements for private endpoint POC — playbook and next steps

Ravi / Aaron — thanks, good questions. Below is the finalized mini-playbook and proposed handoff plan for your firewall team; attaching a single doc "private-endpoint-playbook-v1.md" with the full checklist and test commands.

1) Intermediate NAT support: yes — Redwood supports requests originating from your NAT gateway. For source-based enforcement we prefer tenant-specific client certs or a per-tenant HTTP header (X-Redwood-Tenant) for audit mapping. If you use NAT, ensure the NAT gateway is in the same region as the connector to avoid geo-failover surprises.

2) Ephemeral rotation policy: Redwood will not rotate production pinned egress IPs without 30 days notice. For POC/ephemeral pools we rotate with a 48-hour TTL and publish a versioned manifest at control.redwood-inference.com/egress/{version}.json. We recommend using a DNS approach plus pinned IPs for prod.

3) Auditability and tenant assertion: we support two patterns:
   - Mutual TLS with tenant client certs (strongest) — recommended for regulated workloads.
   - X-Redwood-Tenant header plus signed request IDs in logs (acceptable for many customers).

4) Firewall configuration summary (minimal):
   - Allow outbound TCP/443 to the control plane IPs in egress-ip-manifest.csv.
   - Allow DNS (UDP 53) to your resolver and ensure low TTLs for A/AAAA records we publish.
   - Add telemetry FQDNs to an expanded allowlist if you want direct Redwood telemetry ingestion.

5) Test plan & ops window: 
   - Change window: May 22, 10:00–11:00 PDT. Run connectivity script (included).
   - Verification steps: TLS handshake fingerprint, X-Redwood-Tenant validation, model fetch success (200), and sample inference run.

Next steps: 1) Confirm the change window and NAT disposition, 2) we will attach client cert provisioning docs if you choose mTLS, 3) we will provide a signed attestation post-window with connectivity hashes for your archive.

If that works, let's lock the slot. I can join the window and help validate traces.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
PM, Integrations — Redwood Inference
